newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Cophil unveils new acquisition plans.
newsitem.headline: Cophil unveils new acquisition plans.

text.p: Oil explorer Cophil Exploration Corp said in a notice to the Philippine Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) it was in negotiations for the acquisition of a stake in a bank, a petrochemical firm and a steel firm.

"... Serious negotiations are ongoing for the acquisition by the company of up to 50 percent of Express Savings Bank and up to 10 percent of Petrochemicals Corporation of Asia Pacific," the notice, a copy of which was released by the SEC on Thursday, said.
"Preliminary negotiations have also been commenced for the acquisition of a minority interest in a low-cost housing project and in National Steel Corporation."
The bank and the petrochemicals firm are unlisted while the recently privatised National Steel Corp is majority owned by Malaysia's Wing Tiek Bhd.
Cophil said stockholders on Monday approved the change in the firm's primary purpose which was oil exploration.

The new business plan includes going into property development, banking and other financial services, it said, adding it was not relinquishing oil exploration and related activities but will relegate these to secondary purposes.
Stockholders also approved a change in name to Forum Pacific Inc, "or such similar name containing the word 'Forum' as the SEC shall approve".
Cophil is the main operator of the Manila Bay oil and gas drilling project in which it has a 27.5 percent stake.
Other partners in the project are Coplex Resources NL, Pacrim Energy and Oriental Petroleum and Mineral Corp.
British Gas had an option to buy 25 percent in the project but opted not to take it.
The drilling consortium has explored the area twice but did not make a commercial discovery.
